Each entry names one proper by mass key, form label and proper name, and carries
the `translations` array verbatim into that proper. The array holds exactly the
keys `check-calendar-masses` validates, so the merge copies a structure and does
not translate between schemas. Two routes reach this file and an entry states which one it is on.

Most entries are `project-created` and name no `source_id`, because the project
is its own witness; the witness fields beside the array (`ancient_witness`,
`witness_edition_id`, `witness_artifact_id`, `match_coverage`, `relation`,
`divergence`, `ancient_reading`) are evidence for the entry and are not part of
what merges.

The rest are ANTECEDENT entries, marked by `witness_relation = "antecedent"`, a
`witness` naming a declared `[[sources]]` row, and a `witness_note`. The Missale
Romanum 2002 is in copyright and is not held here, so no entry in this file is a
translation of it. An antecedent entry prints the English a public-domain book
made for an OLDER liturgical text that a historical comparison associated with
this stable slot: the oration entries use an 1861 lay missal, and the sequences use
sequences from Caswall's 1849 *Lyra Catholica*. Its `witness_note` states that
recorded comparison and every difference then observed. On 2026-08-27 every
full `antecedent_latin_here` body was removed from this inventory along with
the postconciliar calendar's bodies. These records are evidence/search leads;
they do not establish a target-edition transcription source or exactness. The English is the
antecedent's, never the reform's, and a page showing it must say so. These rows
carry `rights = "public-domain"` and the `source_id` of the printing the words
were read out of, which is the one thing the project-created rows never carry.

Two ids and what each one is for, because conflating them is how this file
served 63 translations with no attribution and no caution for the length of a
branch. `witness` names a `[[sources]]` row of THIS file by its `id`; the row is
a BOOK, and `source_attestation_problems` in check-calendar-masses holds it to
the act history by that id. `witness_relation` says what the entry is doing with
that book, and `antecedent` is a relation between two Latin texts, not a
printing -- there is no antecedent edition of anything. The two were once run
together as a single invented witness id, `cummiskey-1861-antecedent`, which no
`[[sources]]` row declared and which therefore resolved nowhere: the act-history
cross-check never engaged, and the browser's witness manifest, which keys these
rows by `source_id`, found no row and printed a bare dotted id in place of a
label with `caution` left null. Never encode a relation in a witness id. Declare
the book and state the relation beside it.

Check `incipit` against the target proper before merging. An entry whose mass,
form, proper or incipit no longer answers the target is stale and must be
re-derived, never merged on the strength of its mass key alone.

`untranslated` merges nothing. It is the ledger of propers deliberately left
without English, each with the reason it was left, so that a proper carrying no
`translations` key can be told from one nobody reached, and so a page can say
that no English is recorded rather than showing Latin as though it were the
answer.

after.attests_basis:
The book names no Latin exemplar. It does carry an approbation: its title matter
reads PUBLISHED WITH THE APPROBATION OF THE RIGHT REV. THE BISHOP OF
PHILADELPHIA, which the edition record under
src/sources/works/eugene-cummiskey/roman-missal-english-laity/ quotes in full.
That is a diocesan leave to print, not a promulgation. It revises nothing and
names no printing, so it makes this book no station in the descent of the rite
and tells nobody which Latin printing was on the translator's desk.

The edge therefore rests on the date alone: 1861 falls after Urban VIII's
revision of 1634 and before Divino afflatu of 1911, and the state it can be
translating is the one si-quid-est-1634 left. That is a weak edge and is
labelled as such. The act history holds this same book on these same two values,
and `source_attestation_problems` in check-calendar-masses refuses a source row
that contradicts the act history about a witness both files hold, so this is a
checked restatement of that record and not a second opinion. The sibling row in
roman-1962-proper-translations-v1.toml states the same edge in the same terms
and for the same reason.

What that edge settles is the one thing THIS calendar needed settled, and it is
the whole reason a row for this book can stand in a postconciliar file at all. A
date bound at si-quid-est-1634 places this book's English a century before
sacrosanctum-concilium-1963 and missale-romanum-1969, so it attests a state of
the rite the reform had not yet touched, and it follows that no word quoted from
it is a word of the Missale Romanum 2002. That is the converse of an ordinary
witness claim: this book is cited here BECAUSE it cannot be witnessing the
current Missal. What it can and cannot supply for a given prayer is argued entry
by entry in `witness_note` from the two Latin texts, never from this row.
after.caution: A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book, and under this calendar it stands further off still: what it prints is the English of an ANTECEDENT prayer, not of the Missale Romanum 2002, whose English is the International Commission on English in the Liturgy's and is not carried here in whole or in part. Its slot relation is a documented historical comparison, with source and edition limits stated per entry; it is not current target-edition attestation. Its rubrics, its calendar and its sanctoral are not this calendar's, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

after.rights_basis: Published in the United States in 1861, so in the public domain there by publication date: every United States work published before 1930 has entered the public domain and no renewal question arises for an 1861 imprint. The translator is unnamed and no proprietor survives. The basis is a United States one and is recorded as such, because a public-domain claim does not travel of itself; a reader outside the United States must establish the position in their own jurisdiction. That basis covers the 1861 book's own English, which is what the entries resting on this row carry. It does not cover the Internet Archive text layer some of that English was read out of: `artifact_id` names a remote, unretained artifact whose own rights the source library records as unresolved, those exact bytes being a Google-produced derivative carrying Google's front matter for which no distribution grant was established. The artifact record pins the bytes by sha256 and byte count and gives the URL, so a reader can fetch the same file and check any entry against it; this repository does not redistribute them. Nothing on this row is offered under CC BY 4.0 and this project claims no exclusive right in the wording.
after.role:
NOT a witness to this calendar's Missal, and it must never be read as one. The
Missale Romanum 2002 is in copyright and is not held in this repository, so no
entry in this file reproduces its English or claims to.

What the entries resting on this row publish is the English this book made
for an ANTECEDENT oration. Each such entry's `witness_note` preserves the
historical comparison that selected the stable slot and lists the differences
then observed. The compared postconciliar bodies are no longer resident, so
these notes are audit/search leads rather than current target-edition
attestation. The
relation is a property of the entry, not of the book -- a book cannot be an
antecedent of anything -- which is why it is recorded on each entry as
`witness_relation` and not smuggled into this row's `id`. Until 2026-08-20 it
was smuggled: every one of these entries named a witness `cummiskey-1861-antecedent`
that no row declared, so the browser's witness manifest, which keys these rows by
`source_id`, found no row at all and served 63 translations under a bare dotted
id with no label and no caution.

Standing of the readings is now machine-readable rather than inferred from this
prose. Every retained entry carries an exact `artifact_id` / `passage_id` /
`ia_leaf_range` page-image binding and an independent `publication_artifact_id`
/ `publication_artifact_sha256` / `publication_passage_id` triple selecting one
complete TSV body. Light, truncated, overbroad, and substantively divergent
candidates are text-free `[[untranslated]]` rows instead of positive entries.

This row answers for the ENGLISH and for nothing else. The Latin identity that
licenses each quotation is argued in the entry, and some entries argue it partly
from a third book -- the 1862 Pustet Latin printing, for the days where it is
what shows the older oration standing on that day. That book is evidence about
Latin. It supplies no word of English here and is not a witness on this row.

after.attests_basis:
THIS IS NOT A MISSAL AND WITNESSES NO PRINTING OF ONE. It is a verse translation
of the hymns and sequences of the Roman Breviary and Missal, published at London
in 1849 with no imprimatur, no approbation and no decree in the front matter read
here. It names no Latin exemplar and it prints no Latin beside the English, so it
cannot say which book was on the translator's desk, and its English never had and
does not now have any liturgical standing.

The edge therefore rests on the date alone, which is the weakest kind and is
labelled as such, on the same footing as roman-missal-laity-1806, cummiskey-1843
and cummiskey-1861 in roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml. 1849 falls after Urban VIII's
revision of 1634 and before Divino afflatu of 1911, so the state of the Roman
books it can be translating is the one si-quid-est-1634 left. It is drawn only
because a date bound is a real bound.

WHAT THE DATE BOUND IS WORTH FOR THESE FIVE TEXTS, and it is worth more here than
it would be for an oration: no act between 1634 and 1962 altered the words of
Victimae paschali laudes, Veni Sancte Spiritus, Lauda Sion Salvatorem or Dies
irae, and the Stabat Mater was appointed as a sequence in 1727, more than a
century before this book. The strophe-for-strophe correspondence against the
Latin this repository carries was counted for each of the five and is recorded in
the transcription artifact. So the recension question that governs the 1861
witness's Holy Week does not arise for this material -- which is a statement
about these five texts and must not be generalised to anything else in this book.
after.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts. The active overlay records the
maintainer's choice of Caswall as the through-line across the relevant texts;
it does not argue that Caswall is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

after.rights_basis:
Published at London in 1849, so out of United States copyright on the pre-1931
line, AS DERIVED FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2026 and not as a standing rule: on 1 January
2027 the line becomes before 1932 and a later reader must re-derive it rather
than quote this sentence. This is a foreign publication, so the term cannot be
followed to its end from a domestic registration; the age line is the whole of
the case and is stated as such. Restoration under 17 U.S.C. 104A reaches only
works still protected in the source country on 1 January 1996, and United Kingdom
protection for Edward Caswall, who died in 1878, ended in 1948, so nothing was
restored. The basis is a United States one and a reader elsewhere must establish
the position in their own jurisdiction.

That covers the 1849 book's own English, which is what this file carries. The
`artifact_id` names a project transcription made from the item's page images and
holding nothing but that English; the item's OCR text layer is registered
separately, was used as a finding aid only, and supplied no word recorded here.
NOT RELIED ON: that the Internet Archive item is available, that the download
succeeded, or that the item carries a Public Domain Mark 1.0 licence URL, which
it does.

before.attests_basis:
THIS IS NOT A MISSAL AND WITNESSES NO PRINTING OF ONE. It is a verse translation
of the hymns and sequences of the Roman Breviary and Missal, published at London
in 1849 with no imprimatur, no approbation and no decree in the front matter read
here. It names no Latin exemplar and it prints no Latin beside the English, so it
cannot say which book was on the translator's desk, and its English never had and
does not now have any liturgical standing.

The edge therefore rests on the date alone, which is the weakest kind and is
labelled as such, on the same footing as roman-missal-laity-1806, cummiskey-1843
and cummiskey-1861 in roman-holy-week-acts-v1.toml. 1849 falls after Urban VIII's
revision of 1634 and before Divino afflatu of 1911, so the state of the Roman
books it can be translating is the one si-quid-est-1634 left. It is drawn only
because a date bound is a real bound.

WHAT THE DATE BOUND IS WORTH FOR THESE FIVE TEXTS, and it is worth more here than
it would be for an oration: no act between 1634 and 1962 altered the words of
Victimae paschali laudes, Veni Sancte Spiritus, Lauda Sion Salvatorem or Dies
irae, and the Stabat Mater was appointed as a sequence in 1727, more than a
century before this book. The strophe-for-strophe correspondence against the
Latin this repository carries was counted for each of the five and is recorded in
the transcription artifact. So the recension question that governs the 1861
witness's Holy Week does not arise for this material -- which is a statement
about these five texts and must not be generalised to anything else in this book.
before.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts. The active overlay records the
maintainer's choice of Caswall as the through-line across the relevant texts;
it does not argue that Caswall is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.
before.label: Lyra Catholica: containing all the Breviary and Missal hymns, with others from various sources, translated by Edward Caswall (London: James Burns, 1849)
before.rights_basis:
Published at London in 1849, so out of United States copyright on the pre-1931
line, AS DERIVED FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2026 and not as a standing rule: on 1 January
2027 the line becomes before 1932 and a later reader must re-derive it rather
than quote this sentence. This is a foreign publication, so the term cannot be
followed to its end from a domestic registration; the age line is the whole of
the case and is stated as such. Restoration under 17 U.S.C. 104A reaches only
works still protected in the source country on 1 January 1996, and United Kingdom
protection for Edward Caswall, who died in 1878, ended in 1948, so nothing was
restored. The basis is a United States one and a reader elsewhere must establish
the position in their own jurisdiction.

That covers the 1849 book's own English, which is what this file carries. The
`artifact_id` names a project transcription made from the item's page images and
holding nothing but that English; the item's OCR text layer is registered
separately, was used as a finding aid only, and supplied no word recorded here.
NOT RELIED ON: that the Internet Archive item is available, that the download
succeeded, or that the item carries a Public Domain Mark 1.0 licence URL, which
it does.

before.attests_basis:
Every chant sheet in ICEL's Music for the Roman Missal library carries at the
foot of every page the notice "The English translation and chants of The Roman
Missal © 2010, International Commission on English in the Liturgy
Corporation. All rights reserved." That is the rightsholder's own statement
that these are the words of the Roman Missal, and the act history carries the
Latin state those words translate as `reimpressio-emendata-2008`, the 2008
emended reprinting of the third typical edition. The edge is drawn on each
document's own page statement and on nothing else, which is why
`attests_kind` is `title-page-statement` and not the printing itself: these
are chant sheets, not typical editions.

WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT ATTEST. The chant sheets are tone settings for cantors
and celebrants, not a missal and not an excerpt of the Proper of Time in the
ordinary sense. They carry the English of the ceremonial items they set --
solemn intercessions, the Showing of the Holy Cross, the Exsultet, the Litany
of the Saints, blessings of fire and water -- but set to chant, with
syllabification, neumes, and pointing marks that are performance notation and
not orthography. They must never be cited as the Missal itself or as a ritual
edition.

ICEL's standing grant permits approved, recognized, and promulgated ICEL text

not a grant to retain the wording in Git source, a corpus, generated or
downloadable data, an installed artifact, or a PDF. This inventory therefore
retains only text-free identity, rights, artifact, locator, and SHA-256 audit
metadata. The grant and its limits are recorded with citations in

what_is_published.after:
Two routes publish English here and their tests are different. This section
states the first; `what_is_published_by_the_antecedent_route` states the second.
Neither route supplies the approved English of the Roman Missal. The
project-created route supplies original study English of independently
established public-domain expression; a finite target-edition comparison is
identified only where actually performed. The antecedent route supplies the
historical human translator's words. No ICEL wording is retained or reproduced.

THE PROJECT-CREATED ROUTE. Study English is published for a prayer or chant
only where its Latin adds nothing to the independently established ancient or
public-domain witness that could be anyone's authorship. Three relations
qualify, and each entry says which it is.

`verbatim` -- the two texts differ only in orthography, punctuation, word order,
or demonstrable optical damage. The English renders both.

`abridged` -- the missal drops words the ancient book has and adds none. An
omission is not authorship, so the English still renders only public-domain
words. `divergence` says exactly what was dropped.

`variant` -- the missal substitutes a word or two, or changes an inflection.
`divergence` quotes both readings and says which the English follows, which is
always the missal's, so that the English and the Latin beside it on the page
answer each other. A substitution of one or two words is too small to be
protected expression, and the entry shows the whole of it rather than asserting
it.

Everything else -- a recomposition, a centonisation, a rewriting, a prayer with
no ancient witness in the boundary at all -- is untranslated, and says so.

Where the line falls is this project's judgement. It was made conservatively and
it is shown in full; a reader who disagrees with any single entry can see
precisely what was judged and reach their own answer.

after.attests_basis:
The book names no Latin exemplar. It does carry an approbation: its title matter
reads PUBLISHED WITH THE APPROBATION OF THE RIGHT REV. THE BISHOP OF
PHILADELPHIA, which the edition record under
src/sources/works/eugene-cummiskey/roman-missal-english-laity/ quotes in full.
That is a diocesan leave to print, and it is the same kind of front matter the
1962 Benziger witness carries under Francis Cardinal Spellman -- an ordinary
approving a book for publication in his diocese, not a promulgation. It revises
nothing and names no printing, so it makes this book no station in the descent
of the rite and tells nobody which Latin printing was on the translator's desk.

The edge therefore rests on the date alone: 1861 falls after Urban VIII's
revision of 1634 and before Divino afflatu of 1911, and the state it can be
translating is the one si-quid-est-1634 left. That is a weak edge and is
labelled as such, on the same footing as roman-missal-laity-1806 and

books it can be translating is the one si-quid-est-1634 left. It is drawn only
because a date bound is a real bound.

WHAT THE DATE BOUND IS WORTH FOR THESE FIVE TEXTS, and it is worth more here than
it would be for an oration: no act between 1634 and 1962 altered the words of
Victimae paschali laudes, Veni Sancte Spiritus, Lauda Sion Salvatorem or Dies
irae, and the Stabat Mater was appointed as a sequence in 1727, more than a
century before this book. The strophe-for-strophe correspondence against the
Latin this repository carries was counted for each of the five and is recorded in
the transcription artifact. So the recension question that governs the 1861
witness's Holy Week does not arise for this material -- which is a statement
about these five texts and must not be generalised to anything else in this book.
before.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts. The active overlay records the
maintainer's choice of Caswall as the through-line across all five and Irons as
an alternative for the Dies irae; it does not argue that either voice is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

translations.text: Brothers: knowing that it is now time for us to rise from sleep. For our salvation is now nearer than when we came to believe. The night has passed, and the day has drawn near. So let us cast away the works of darkness and put on the armor of light. Let us walk honorably, as in the day: not in revelry and drunkenness, not in sexual indulgence and shameless acts, not in strife and jealousy, but put on the Lord Jesus Christ.

Alleluia, alleluia. V. Hail, Mary, full of grace: the Lord is with you; blessed are you among women. Alleluia. V. The rod of Jesse has blossomed: the Virgin has borne God and man. God has restored peace, reconciling in himself things below with things above. Alleluia.
Alleluia, alleluia. V. Show me your face; let your voice sound in my ears, for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely. Alleluia.

You are the glory of Jerusalem, you are the joy of Israel, you are the honor of our people. V. You are wholly beautiful, Mary, and the stain of original sin is not in you. V. Blessed are you, holy Virgin Mary, most worthy of every praise, who crushed the serpent's head with your virgin foot.
Alleluia, alleluia. V. Mary has been assumed into heaven; the host of angels rejoices. Alleluia.
Alleluia, alleluia. V. The solemnity of the glorious Virgin Mary, of the seed of Abraham, sprung from the tribe of Judah, illustrious in the line of David. Alleluia.

God, whose Only Begotten, through his life, death, and resurrection, won for us the rewards of eternal salvation, grant, we ask, that as we recall these mysteries in the most sacred Rosary of the Blessed Virgin Mary, we may both imitate what they contain and attain what they promise. Through the same Lord.

Let us all rejoice in the Lord as we celebrate the feast in honor of the blessed Virgin Mary, at whose solemnity the angels rejoice and join in praising the Son of God. My heart has uttered a good word: I speak my works to the King. V. Glory to the Father.
Most worthy Queen of the world, Mary ever Virgin, intercede for our peace and salvation, you who bore Christ the Lord, the Savior of all. (In Paschal time, Alleluia.)

text_structure.checked: 1962 target facsimile artifact622/printed541 unit2694, page images at200 and400dpi read2026-10-29; original study English renders the same printed conditional rubric.

translations.text: Mary, sprung from royal lineage, shines forth; we ask most devoutly in mind and spirit to be helped by her prayers. (In Paschal time, Alleluia.)

text_structure.checked: Exact source-owned conditional Paschal invocation marked as a rubric action; preserve the whole literal span, with Alleluia selected only in its Paschal context.

translations.text: God, who gave blessed Peter, your Apostle, the keys of the heavenly kingdom and entrusted him with the pontifical authority to bind and loose, grant that, with the help of his intercession, we may be freed from the bonds of our sins.
May the gift offered bring us joy, Lord, so that, just as we proclaim how wondrous you are in your Apostle Peter, so through him we may receive the abundance of your pardon.
Lord, we ask that the prayer of blessed Peter the Apostle may commend the prayers and sacrificial offerings of your Church, so that what we celebrate for his glory may help us obtain pardon.

Lord God, who use the ministry of priests in bringing your peoples to new birth, grant us persevering service in your will, so that, by the gift of your grace, the people consecrated to you may increase in our days both in merits and in number. Through the Lord.
Grant, Lord, we ask, that, as we pass from old things to new, so, putting off the old condition, we may be renewed in minds made holy. Through the Lord.
Lord, we ask that the power of this sacrifice may mercifully wipe away our old condition and increase renewal and salvation within us. Through our Lord.

O God, you gladden us with the annual solemnity of blessed Alexius your Confessor. Mercifully grant that we may also imitate the deeds of the one whose birthday feast we celebrate. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. R. Amen.

Nourished by sharing in the sacred gift, we ask, Lord our God, that through the intercession of blessed Boniface, your Martyr, we may experience the effect of what we celebrate in worship. Through the Lord.
Lord, through receiving your sacrament, may we be both cleansed of our hidden sins and freed from the snares of our enemies. Through the Lord.
God, you gladden us with the annual celebration of blessed Eusebius, your Confessor; graciously grant that, as we celebrate his anniversary, we may follow his examples toward you. Through the Lord.
Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who celebrate the anniversary feast of blessed Mennas, your martyr, may through his intercession be strengthened in love for your name. Through our Lord.
Hear us, O God our Savior, so that, as we rejoice in the feast of blessed Praxedes your Virgin, we may likewise be schooled in a spirit of reverent devotion. Through our Lord.
Lord, we ask that the intercession of blessed Sabbas the abbot may commend us to you, so that through his protection we may attain what we cannot achieve by our own merits. Through our Lord.

[\"comm-s-sabbae-abbatis\",\"main\",\"Po.translation_note: Conversationis ejus ... insignia is rendered as 'what distinguished his way of life'; no particular virtues or deeds are supplied.

translations.text: Lord, may blessed Sabbas protect us, together with the reception of your sacrament, by interceding for us, so that we may experience what distinguished his way of life and receive the help of his intercession. Through the Lord.

[\"comm-s-sabbae-abbatis\",\"main\",\"Se.translation_note: The conclusion is translated only through the printed Qui tecum; its incomplete English syntax preserves the source abbreviation.

translations.text: Lord, we ask that Saint Sabbas may earnestly plead that the sacrificial offerings placed upon the holy altars may bring us salvation. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son: who with you.

Eternal Shepherd, look graciously upon your flock, and keep it under your perpetual protection through blessed Sylvester, Supreme Pontiff, whom you appointed shepherd of the whole Church. Through our Lord.

Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we who celebrate the birthday feast of blessed Thecla, your virgin and martyr, may both rejoice in her yearly solemnity and grow through the example of such great faith. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

Eternal Shepherd, look graciously upon your flock, and keep it under your perpetual protection through blessed Zephyrinus, your Martyr and Supreme Pontiff, whom you appointed shepherd of the whole Church. Through the Lord.
Remember, Virgin Mother of God, when you stand in the Lord’s presence, to speak for our good, so that he may turn his wrath away from us.
We ask, Lord, that the sacrifice of your people, solemnly offered at the anniversary feast of your holy martyrs Chrysanthus and Daria, may be pleasing to you. Through the Lord.
Grant us, we pray, Lord, through the intercession of your holy martyrs Cyprian and Justina, to receive with pure minds what we touch with our mouths. Through the Lord.

God, who give us joy in the yearly solemn celebration of your holy Martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, mercifully grant that we may be set aflame by the examples of those in whose merits we rejoice. Through our Lord.
Lord, may this communion cleanse us of sin and, through the intercession of your holy Martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, make us sharers in the heavenly remedy. Through the Lord.
Be appeased, we ask, Lord, by the gifts offered, and through the intercession of your holy Martyrs defend us from every danger. Through the Lord.

Almighty God, we pray, grant that the festive solemnity of your holy martyrs Maurice and his companions may gladden us, so that we may glory in the birthday feasts of those on whose intercession we rely. Through the Lord.
God, you grant us to celebrate the birthday feasts of your holy martyrs Placid and his companions; grant us to rejoice in their company in eternal blessedness. Through the Lord.

Grant us, we pray, Lord, through the intercession of your holy martyrs Placid and his companions, to receive with pure minds what we touch with our mouths. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

Grant us, we ask, Lord our God, to venerate with unceasing devotion the palms of victory of your holy virgins and martyrs Ursula and her companions, so that, since we cannot celebrate them with a worthy mind, we may at least honor them assiduously with humble acts of service. Through the Lord.
Grant us, we ask, Lord, through the intercession of your holy virgins and martyrs Ursula and her companions, to receive with a pure mind what we touch with our mouth. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Look, we ask, Lord, upon the gifts set on your altars for the feast of your holy virgins and martyrs Ursula and her companions, so that, as through these blessed mysteries you bestowed glory on them, you may likewise grant us forgiveness. Through the Lord.
God, you allow us to celebrate the anniversaries of your holy Martyrs Sixtus, Felicissimus and Agapitus; grant us joy in their company in eternal blessedness. Through our Lord.
Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. Saint Paul the Apostle, preacher of truth and teacher of the nations, intercede for us. Alleluia.

O God, you taught a multitude of nations through the preaching of blessed Paul the Apostle. Grant us, we ask, that we may experience before you the patronage of the one whose birthday feast we celebrate.
Lord, having received the sacraments, we pray, with blessed Paul your Apostle interceding, that what has been celebrated for his glory may bring us healing.

Through the prayers of your Apostle Paul, Lord, sanctify your people's gifts, so that these gifts, pleasing to you by your own institution, may become still more pleasing through the patronage of him who pleads.
Alleluia, alleluia. V. You are a priest for ever, according to the order of Melchizedek. Alleluia. V. This is the priest whom the Lord has crowned. Alleluia.
So that your sacrifices may bring us salvation, Lord, we ask that blessed N., your Confessor and a distinguished Doctor, may come forward to intercede. Through the Lord.

Alleluia, alleluia. V. In your splendor and beauty, press forward; advance prosperously and reign. Alleluia. V. For the sake of truth, gentleness, and justice; and your right hand will guide you wonderfully. Alleluia.

Alleluia, alleluia. V. In your splendor and beauty, press forward; advance prosperously and reign. Alleluia. V. For the sake of truth, gentleness, and justice; and your right hand will guide you wonderfully. Alleluia.

Since Thy Church has been nourished by the sacred repast, govern her in Thy clemency, we beseech Thee, O Lord, so that under the guidance of Thy mighty rule she may enjoy greater freedom and abiding integrity of religion. Through our Lord.

translations.text: In Thy loving kindness, we beseech Thee, O Lord, be moved by the offering of our gifts and enlighten Thy Church: that Thy flock may prosper everywhere and the shepherds, under Thy guidance, may be rendered acceptable to Thee. Through our Lord.

translations.text: Graciously accept, Lord, the sacrifices dedicated to you in honor of the merits of blessed N., your Martyr and Bishop, and grant that they may provide us with lasting help. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.
God, who taught the whole world through the preaching of blessed Paul the Apostle, grant, we ask, that we who honor his conversion today may walk toward you by following the examples he set.
Sanctified by the saving mystery, Lord, we ask that we may not lack the prayer of the one under whose protection you have given us guidance.
Through the prayers of your Apostle Paul, Lord, sanctify your people's gifts, so that what is pleasing to you by your own ordinance may become more pleasing through the advocacy of the one who prays.
Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. Holy Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle, so that we may not perish at the fearful judgment. Alleluia.

[\"easter-vigil\",\"main\",\"Litany of t.proper: Litany of the Saints, first part

translations.text:
Lord, have mercy.
Christ, have mercy.
Lord, have mercy.
Christ, hear us.
Christ, heed us.
God the Father in heaven, have mercy on us.
God the Son, Redeemer of the world, have mercy on us.
God the Holy Spirit, have mercy on us.
Holy Trinity, one God, have mercy on us.
Holy Mary, pray for us.
Holy Mother of God, pray.
Holy Virgin of virgins, pray.
Saint Michael, pray.
Saint Gabriel, pray.
Saint Raphael, pray.
All holy angels and archangels, pray for us.
All holy orders of blessed spirits, pray.
Saint John the Baptist, pray.
Saint Joseph, pray.
All holy patriarchs and prophets, pray.
Saint Peter, pray.
Saint Paul, pray.
Saint Andrew, pray.
Saint John, pray.
All holy apostles and evangelists, pray.
All holy disciples of the Lord, pray.
Saint Stephen, pray.
Saint Lawrence, pray.
Saint Vincent, pray.
All holy martyrs, pray.
Saint Sylvester, pray.
Saint Gregory, pray.
Saint Augustine, pray.
All holy bishops and confessors, pray.
All holy teachers, pray.
Saint Anthony, pray.
Saint Benedict, pray.
Saint Dominic, pray.
Saint Francis, pray.
All holy priests and Levites, pray.
All holy monks and hermits, pray.
Saint Mary Magdalene, pray.
Saint Agnes, pray.
Saint Cecilia, pray.
Saint Agatha, pray.
Saint Anastasia, pray.
All holy virgins and widows, pray.
All holy men and women of God, intercede for us.

[\"easter-vigil\",\"main\",\"Litany of t.proper: Litany of the Saints, second part
[\"easter-vigil\",\"main\",\"Litany of t.translation_note: The abbreviated response 'libera' is rendered only as 'deliver'; 'us, Lord' is not supplied. 'Hear us' is included only where audi nos is printed. Domnum apostolicum is translated as the title 'the apostolic lord' without replacing it with a personal name.

translations.text:
Be gracious; spare us, Lord.
Be gracious; answer us, Lord.
From every evil, deliver us, Lord.
From every sin, deliver.
From everlasting death, deliver.
Through the mystery of your holy incarnation, deliver.
Through your coming, deliver.
Through your birth, deliver.
Through your baptism and holy fasting, deliver.
Through your cross and passion, deliver.
Through your death and burial, deliver.
Through your holy resurrection, deliver.
Through your wondrous ascension, deliver.
Through the coming of the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, deliver.
On the day of judgment, deliver.
We sinners ask you: hear us.
Spare us, we ask you: hear us.
Graciously govern and preserve your holy Church, we ask you: hear us.
Graciously keep the pope and all ecclesiastical orders in holy religion, we ask you.
Graciously humble the enemies of holy Church, we ask you.
Graciously give peace and true harmony to Christian kings and princes, we ask you.
Graciously strengthen and preserve us ourselves in your holy service, we ask you.
Repay all our benefactors with everlasting good things, we ask you.
Graciously give and preserve the fruits of the earth, we ask you.
Graciously give eternal rest to all the faithful departed, we ask you.
Graciously answer us, we ask you.
Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, spare us, Lord.
Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, answer us, Lord.
Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.
Christ, hear us.
Christ, answer us.

Pour into us, Lord, the Spirit of your love, so that in your loving kindness you may bring into harmony those whom you have satisfied with the paschal sacraments. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the same Holy Spirit, God, for all ages of ages.

[\"easter-vigil\",\"main\",\"Prayer at t.translation_note: In 'fidei ipsius sitis,' ipsius is read as referring to the people being born anew; it can also emphasize faith itself. The supplied Latin's terminal comma is retained.

translations.text: Almighty, everlasting God, look favorably upon the devotion of the people being born anew, who, like a deer, long for the spring of your waters; and graciously grant that the thirst of their faith may sanctify soul and body through the mystery of baptism. Through Christ our Lord,
Grant, we ask, almighty God, that with purified minds we may understand what we celebrate in solemn worship. Through the Lord.
Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. Sweet wood, bearing sweet nails and sweet burdens: you alone were worthy to support the King and Lord of heaven. Alleluia.
By the sign of the Cross, deliver us from our enemies, our God.

But we ought to glory in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, in whom are our salvation, life, and resurrection, through whom we have been saved and set free.
May God have mercy on us and bless us; may he make his face shine upon us and have mercy on us. ℣. Glory to the Father.
Protect your people, Lord, by the sign of the holy Cross from all the snares of all enemies, so that we may render you pleasing service and our sacrifice may be acceptable, alleluia.

Lord, pour into us the Spirit of your love, so that through your loving kindness you may make those whom you have satisfied with the one heavenly bread one in heart. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the same Holy Spirit.

Almighty and eternal God, who prepared in the Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary a worthy dwelling for the Holy Spirit, graciously grant that, as we devoutly celebrate the feast (commemoration) of that same Immaculate Heart, we may be able to live according to your Heart. Through our Lord ... in the unity of the same.

Nourished by divine gifts, Lord, we humbly ask you that, through the intercession of the Blessed Virgin Mary, whose Immaculate Heart we have reverently honored with this solemn celebration (commemoration), we may be freed from present dangers and attain the joys of eternal life. Through the Lord.
As we offer the immaculate Lamb to your majesty, Lord, we ask that the divine fire that ineffably inflamed the Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary may kindle our hearts. Through the same Lord of ours.

Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our fathers. And worthy of praise and glorious for ever.
And blessed is the name of your glory, which is holy. And worthy of praise and glorious for ever.
Blessed are you in the holy temple of your glory. And worthy of praise and glorious for ever.
Blessed are you upon the holy throne of your kingdom. And worthy of praise and glorious for ever.
Blessed are you upon the sceptre of your divinity. And worthy of praise and glorious for ever.
Blessed are you, who sit upon the Cherubim, looking upon the depths. And worthy of praise and glorious for ever.
Blessed are you, who walk upon the wings of the winds and over the waves of the sea. And worthy of praise and glorious for ever.
Let all your angels and saints bless you. And let them praise you and glorify you for ever.
Let the heavens, earth, sea, and all that is in them bless you. And let them praise you and glorify you for ever.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. And worthy of praise and glorious for ever.
As it was in the beginning, and now, and always, and for ever and ever. Amen. And worthy of praise and glorious for ever.
Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our fathers. And worthy of praise and glorious for ever.

I am the salvation of the people, says the Lord: in whatever distress they cry to me, I will hear them; and I will be their Lord for ever. Listen, my people, to my law; incline your ear to the words of my mouth. V. Glory be to the Father.

I saw a man seated on a lofty throne, whom a multitude of angels adores, singing together: behold, the name of his dominion is eternal. Shout joyfully to God, all the earth; serve the Lord with gladness. V. Glory be to the Father.

[\"mass-of-the-lords-supper\",\"main\",\.proper: Hymn at the Translation of the Blessed Sacrament

translations.text:
During the procession, the hymn Pange lingua, gloriosi Corporis mysterium is sung as far as the words Tantum ergo; if needed, the same hymn is repeated.

Tongue, proclaim the mystery
of the glorious Body
and of the precious Blood
which, as the ransom of the world,
the King of the nations,
the fruit of a noble womb, poured out.

Given to us, born for us
from an undefiled Virgin,
and having lived in the world,
after sowing the seed of the word,
he brought his time of dwelling here
to a close in a wondrous order.

During the night of the final supper,
reclining among his brothers,
having fully observed the law
in the foods that the law required,
he gives himself with his own hands
as food for the company of twelve.

The incarnate Word makes real bread
into flesh by his word;
the pure wine becomes Christ's Blood.
If the senses fall short,
faith alone is sufficient
to make the sincere heart firm.

Therefore, let us bow in reverence
before so great a Sacrament.
Let the ancient observance
yield to the new rite;
may faith supply
what our senses lack.

To the Father and to the Son
be praise and joyful acclaim,
salvation, honor, power,
and blessing as well;
to the One who proceeds from both
let equal praise be given.
Amen.

actions.text: During the procession, the hymn Pange lingua, gloriosi Corporis mysterium is sung as far as the words Tantum ergo; if needed, the same hymn is repeated.

text_structure.checked: The leading instruction is a nonspoken action. The following six hymn paragraph groups, including final Amen, are freshly translated from the complete source-owned Latin.

translations.text:
Where are charity and love, God is there. V. The love of Christ hath gathered us together. V. Let us exult and be joyful in Him. V. Let us fear and love the living God. V. And let us love one another with sincere hearts.

Ant. Where are charity and love, God is there. V. Being, therefore, assembled together. V. Let us beware of being divided in mind. V. Let malicious upbraidings cease, let wranglings cease. V. And may Christ, our God, be in the midst of us.

Ant. Where are charity and love, God is there. V. Together with the blessed, too, may we see. V. Thy face in glory, O Christ, God. V. Which is infinitely noble joy. V. Through endless ages of ages. Amen.

[\"mass-of-the-lords-supper\",\"main\",\.witness_note: Historical three-strophe text; the antiphon repetitions are retained as printed.

translations.text:
Be present, Lord, we ask, in the duty of our service; and because you deigned to wash your disciples' feet, do not disdain the works of your hands, which you commanded us to keep, so that, just as outward stains are washed away here for us and by us, so the inward sins of us all may be washed away by you. May you yourself be pleased to grant this, you who live and reign for ages of ages.
R. Amen.
Blessed is the womb of the Virgin Mary, which carried the Son of the eternal Father, alleluia.

Hail, holy Mother, who have given birth to the King, who rules heaven and earth for ever and ever, alleluia, alleluia. My heart has poured out a good word: I recount my works to the King.
V. Glory to the Father.

May the humanity of your Only Begotten come to our aid, Lord, so that Jesus Christ our Lord, who was born of the Virgin and did not impair his mother’s integrity but consecrated it, may make our offering acceptable to you at the solemn celebration of her Nativity, freeing us from our sins. He lives and reigns with you in unity.

Lord, we ask that our gifts may prove fitting for the mysteries of today’s Nativity and always fill us with peace, so that, as the one born a man also shone forth as God, so this earthly substance may impart to us what is divine. Through the same Jesus Christ our Lord.

Almighty, everlasting God, who made our Savior take flesh and undergo the cross so that the human race might have an example of humility to imitate, graciously grant that we may merit both the lessons of his endurance and a share in his resurrection. Through the same Lord.

Glory, praise, and honor to Thee, O Christ, our King!
Hosanna, children winsome to Thee, Redeemer, sing.
R. Glory, etc.

Thou art the King of Israel, of David's glorious line,
In the name of God Thou comest, Thou blessed King divine.
R. Glory, etc.

Thy praises loud in heaven each host angelic sings,
And mortal man in unison with all created things.
R. Glory, etc.

With palms the Hebrew people went forth to meet their King:
Behold, we, too, our homage and prayers and anthems bring.
R. Glory, etc.

To Thee about to suffer, they paid their debt of praise;
To Thee on throne exalted, we now our voices raise.
R. Glory, etc.

Their homage Thou acceptedst: accept the hearts we bring,
Who all that's good approvest, Thou good and gracious King.
R. Glory, etc.

[\"palm-sunday\",\"main\",\"Hymn to Chri.witness_note: The historical refrain cues are retained as printed and remain unexpanded.

translations.text: With shining palms we bow down before the Lord who comes; let us all go to meet him with hymns and songs, glorifying him and saying: “Blessed is the Lord.”

Hail, our King, Son of David, Redeemer of the world, whom the prophets foretold would come as Savior to the house of Israel. For the Father sent you into the world as a saving victim, whom all the saints awaited from the beginning of the world, and now: “Hosanna to the Son of David. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Hosanna in the highest.”
Almighty God, grant, we ask, that the dignity of the human condition, wounded by excess, may be restored through the diligent practice of healing restraint. Through our Lord.

Moses consecrated the altar to the Lord, offering whole burnt offerings upon it and sacrificing victims; he offered an evening sacrifice as a sweet fragrance to the Lord God, in the sight of the children of Israel.
Make us always have both fear and love of your holy name, Lord, for you never leave without your guidance those whom you establish in the steadfastness of your love. Through our Lord.
May the ears of your mercy be open, Lord, to the prayers of those who plead; and, so that you may grant those who ask what they desire, make them ask for what pleases you. Through our Lord.

Alleluia, alleluia. V. O Lord, how good and gentle your Spirit is within us! Alleluia. (Here one genuflects) V. Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful, and kindle in them the fire of your love.

text_structure.checked: Project study translation carries the separately proved genuflection direction as a rubric, not words said.

[\"pentecost-ember-friday\",\"main\",\"S.translation_note: The printed ellipsis and conclusion ending ejusdem ('of the same') are retained without supplying the omitted words.

translations.text: May that divine fire, which through the Holy Spirit kindled the hearts of the disciples of Christ your Son, consume the sacrifices offered in your sight, Lord. Through the same Lord of ours ... in the unity of the same.
Alleluia, alleluia. V. Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful, and light in them the fire of your love.

Alleluia, alleluia. V. The Apostles were speaking in various tongues of the mighty works of God. Alleluia. (Here one genuflects) V. Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful, and kindle in them the fire of your love.

translations.text: Be present to your people, Lord, we ask, and defend those whom you have imbued with heavenly mysteries from the fury of enemies. Through the Lord.
Graciously sanctify these gifts, Lord, we ask; and, having accepted the offering of the spiritual victim, make us ourselves into a perfect, everlasting gift to you. Through our Lord.

Alleluia, alleluia. V. Send forth your Spirit, and they will be created; and you will renew the face of the earth. Alleluia. (Here one genuflects) V. Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful, and kindle in them the fire of your love.

translations.text: May the offering of the present gift purify us, Lord, we ask, and make us worthy of sacred participation. Through our Lord.

God, you willed that blessed Mary, ever Virgin, the dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, should be presented in the temple on this day. Grant, we ask, that through her intercession we may be found worthy to be presented in the temple of your glory. Through the Lord ... in the unity of the same Holy Spirit.
Alleluia, alleluia. V. The old man carried the Child; the Child in turn ruled the old man. Alleluia.
I invoke the living God himself, who was pleased to heal me of every wound and restore my breast to my chest.

Let us all rejoice in the Lord, celebrating a feast day in honor of blessed Agatha, Virgin and Martyr. At her passion the angels rejoice and praise the Son of God. My heart overflows with a good word; I speak of my works to the King. ℣. Glory to the Father.

Come, bride of Christ, receive the crown which the Lord has prepared for you for eternity; for love of him you shed your blood. ℣. You have loved justice and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions. ℣. In your splendor and beauty, press onward, advance with success, and reign.

O God, through blessed Alphonsus Mary, your Confessor and Bishop, who burned with zeal for souls, you made your Church fruitful with new offspring. We ask that, instructed by his saving counsels and strengthened by his examples, we may be able to reach you in blessedness. Through the Lord.

[\"s-alfonsi-mariae-ligorio-episcopi-con.translation_note: The Latin leaves the objects of percipiant and collaudent unexpressed; the English likewise keeps them implicit.

translations.text: God, you made blessed Alphonsus Maria, your Confessor and Bishop, a faithful steward and herald of the divine mystery; through his merits and prayers grant that your faithful may both receive often and, through receiving, give praise without end. Through the Lord.

Lord Jesus Christ, burn our hearts with the heavenly fire of sacrifice so that they yield a sweet fragrance, you who granted blessed Alphonsus Maria both to celebrate these mysteries and, through them, to present himself to you as a holy victim. You who live and reign.
Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. The Lord has loved Andrew as a sweet fragrance. Alleluia.

God, who set wondrous ascents to yourself in the heart of blessed Andrew, your confessor, through his demanding vow to advance daily in the virtues, grant that through his merits and intercession we may share in that same grace in such a way that, always doing what is more perfect, we may happily be led to the summit of your glory. Through the Lord.

Lord, we ask that the intercession of blessed Anthony the Abbot may commend us, so that we may attain through his protection what we cannot achieve by our own merits. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

[\"s-antonii-abbatis\",\"main\",\"Postco.translation_note: Conversationis ejus insignia denotes the distinguishing marks or outstanding qualities of his way of life; the translation retains that experiential language rather than replacing it with a request to imitate him.

translations.text: As we receive your sacrament, Lord, may blessed Anthony the Abbot protect us by interceding for us, so that we may both come to know by experience the outstanding qualities of his way of life and receive the help of his intercession. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

Lord, we ask that Saint Anthony the Abbot may plead for the sacrifices placed upon the holy altars to bring us salvation. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

[\"s-antonii-padua-confessoris-ecclesiae.translation_note: Votiva is rendered 'devout' in the phrase solemnitas votiva; no additional votive-Mass appointment is inferred.

translations.text: God, may the devout celebration of the feast of blessed Anthony, your Confessor and Doctor, gladden your Church, so that she may always be strengthened by spiritual help and be worthy to enjoy eternal joys. Through our Lord.
Filled with divine gifts, Lord, we ask that through the merits and intercession of blessed Anthony, your Confessor and Doctor, we may experience the effect of the saving sacrifice. Through the Lord.

Almighty God, grant, we ask, that as we give thanks for the gifts we have received, we may receive greater blessings through the intercession of blessed Antoninus, your Confessor and Bishop. Through our Lord.
Lord, so that your sacrifices may bring us salvation, we ask that blessed Augustine, your Bishop and eminent Doctor, come forward as an intercessor. Through our Lord.

Lord, may we never lack the devout prayer of Saint Augustine, your Bishop and Doctor; may it make our gifts acceptable and always obtain your forgiveness for us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.
Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. The glorious choir of the Apostles praises you, Lord. Alleluia.

[\"s-bartholomaei-apostoli\",\"main\",\".translation_note: The English takes the unexpressed subject of credidit and docuit to be Bartholomew.

translations.text: Almighty, eternal God, you have granted the venerable and holy joy of this day on the feast (commemoration) of your blessed Apostle Bartholomew; grant your Church, we ask, both to love what he believed and to proclaim what he taught. Through the Lord.

Recalling the solemn celebrations (memory) of your blessed Apostle Bartholomew, we ask, Lord, that we may receive your blessings with the help of him in whose honor we offer you sacrifices of praise. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you.

God, you gave blessed Bernard to your people as a minister of eternal salvation; grant, we ask, that we may be worthy to have as our intercessor in heaven the one we had as a teacher of life on earth. Through the Lord.
Lord, so that your sacrifices may bring us salvation, we ask that blessed Bernard, your Confessor and eminent Doctor, come forward as an intercessor. Through our Lord.

Lord, may we never lack the devout prayer of Saint Bernard, your Confessor and Doctor; may it make our gifts acceptable and always obtain your forgiveness for us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

Having been filled by the abundance of the divine gift, we ask, Lord our God, that, through the intercession of blessed Bibiana, your virgin and martyr, we may always live by partaking of it. Through the Lord.

Lord, graciously accept the sacrificial offerings dedicated to you on account of the merits of blessed Bibiana, your virgin and martyr, and grant that they may become an everlasting help to us. Through the Lord.

Lord our God, you revealed heavenly secrets to blessed Bridget through your only-begotten Son; through her devout intercession grant us, your servants, to rejoice with gladness at the revelation of your everlasting glory. Through the same Lord.

O God, you gave your people blessed Bonaventure as a minister of eternal salvation. Grant, we ask, that we may be worthy to have as our intercessor in heaven the one we had as a teacher of life on earth. Through the Lord.
O God, who reward faithful souls, grant that through the prayers of blessed Bonaventure, your Confessor and Bishop, whose revered feast we celebrate, we may obtain forgiveness. Through the Lord.

May the annual solemnity of Saint Bonaventure, your Confessor and Bishop, make us acceptable to your mercy, Lord, we ask, so that through these acts of devout atonement a blessed reward may attend him and the gifts of your grace may be won for us. Through the Lord.

Almighty God, we pray that we who have received heavenly nourishment may, through the intercession of blessed Bruno, your confessor, be fortified by it against every adversity. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

[\"s-camilli-lellis-confessoris\",\"main.translation_note: The final fragment 'who with you' preserves the source's actual abbreviated ending 'Qui tecum.'; no verb or continuation is supplied.

translations.text: May the unblemished sacrifice, by which we renew that work of the boundless love of our Lord Jesus Christ, be, O God, almighty Father, through Saint Camillus's intercession, a saving remedy against all illnesses of body and soul, and comfort and protection in the final struggle. Through the same Jesus Christ our Lord, your Son: who with you.

God, who gave the law to Moses at the summit of Mount Sinai and who, through your holy angels, wondrously placed the body of blessed Catherine, your virgin and martyr, in that same place, grant, we ask, that by her merits and intercession we may be able to reach the mountain that is Christ, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

Eternal Shepherd, look graciously upon your flock, and keep it under your perpetual protection through blessed Clement, your Martyr and Supreme Pontiff, whom you appointed shepherd of the whole Church. Through the Lord.

We ask you, Lord, graciously govern your Church, nourished by this holy refreshment, so that, directed by your mighty rule, she may grow in freedom and persevere in the integrity of religion. Through the Lord.

With these gifts offered, we ask you, Lord, graciously enlighten your Church, so that your flock may make progress everywhere and its shepherds, under your governance, may be pleasing to your name. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

Lord, may blessed Francis, by interceding for us, join the reception of your sacrament in protecting us, so that we may experience the excellence of his way of life and receive the help of his intercession. Through the Lord.

Lord, we pray, may Saint Francis earnestly ask that the sacrificial offerings placed upon the sacred altars bring us salvation. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly delights in his commandments. Alleluia. ℣. The righteous man will spring up like a lily and bloom forever before the Lord. Alleluia.

God, who chose the Archangel Gabriel from among the other angels to announce the mystery of your Incarnation, mercifully grant that we who celebrate his feast (commemoration) on earth may experience his protection in heaven. You who live and reign with God the Father in unity.

God, who gave blessed Gregory to your people as a minister of eternal salvation, grant, we ask, that we may be worthy to have as an intercessor in heaven the one we had as a teacher of life on earth. Through the Lord.
Lord, so that your sacrifices may bring us salvation, we ask that blessed Gregory, your Bishop and eminent Doctor, come forward to intercede. Through the Lord.
Lord, may the devout prayer of Saint Gregory, your Bishop and Doctor, never fail us; may it make our gifts acceptable and always obtain your pardon for us. Through the Lord.
Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the revered feast of blessed Gregory, your confessor and bishop, may increase our devotion and advance our salvation. Through the Lord.

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, as we give thanks for the gifts we have received, we may, through the intercession of blessed Gregory, your confessor and bishop, receive greater benefits. Through our Lord.

God, you gave blessed Hilary to your people as a minister of eternal salvation. Grant, we ask, that we may be found worthy to have as our intercessor in heaven the one we had as a teacher of life on earth. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.
So that your sacrifices may bring us salvation, Lord, we ask that blessed Hilary, your Bishop and a distinguished Doctor, may come forward to intercede. Through our Lord.

Lord, may the devout prayer of Saint Hilary, your Bishop and Doctor, never fail us; may it win acceptance for our gifts and always obtain your forgiveness for us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.
Help us, Lord, we ask, through the intercession of blessed James your Apostle, for whose feast (commemoration) we have joyfully received your holy gifts. Through our Lord.

Nourished by sharing in the sacred gift, we ask, Lord our God, that, through the intercession of blessed Ignatius, your martyr and bishop, we may experience the effect of what we celebrate in worship. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God for ever and ever.
R. Amen.

God, you chose blessed Joachim above all your saints to be the father of your Son's mother; grant, we ask, that, as we honor his feasts (memory), we may also continually experience his protection. Through the same Lord.

Accept, most merciful God, the sacrifice offered to your majesty in honor of the holy Patriarch Joachim, father of Mary the Virgin, so that, through his intercession together with his wife and most blessed child, we may be worthy to attain complete forgiveness of sins and everlasting glory. Through the Lord.

O God, you raised up Saint John, your Confessor, as a father and teacher of young people, and through him, with the Virgin Mary as helper, you willed new religious families to flourish in your Church. Grant, we ask, that, kindled by the same fire of charity, we may be able to seek souls and serve you alone. Through our Lord.

To us who have been filled with the mystery of your Body and Blood, O Lord, grant, we ask, that through the intercession of Saint John the Confessor we may always remain in thanksgiving. You who live and reign with God the Father in unity.

Receive, O Lord, the pure offering of the saving sacrifice, and grant that, loving you in all things and above all things, we may be worthy to live for the praise of your glory. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.
We ask, Lord, that blessed John Chrysostom, your bishop and eminent doctor, may come forward to intercede, so that your sacrifices may bring us salvation. Through the Lord.
May the devout prayer of Saint John Chrysostom, your bishop and doctor, not fail us, Lord; may it both make our gifts acceptable and always obtain your pardon for us. Through our Lord.

Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. The Lord has kept your hand safe for you, because you fight the Lord’s battles. Alleluia. ℣. Blessed is the Lord my God, who trains my hands for combat and my fingers for war. Alleluia.
A tree has hope: if it is cut down, it grows green again, and its branches sprout. Alleluia.
May the intercession of blessed John the Abbot commend us to you, Lord, we ask, so that through his patronage we may attain what we cannot achieve through our own merits. Through our Lord.

As we receive your sacrament, Lord, may blessed John the Abbot protect us by interceding for us, so that we may experience the excellence of his way of life and receive the support of his intercession. Through the Lord.
Lord, we ask that Saint John the Abbot may pray that the sacrificial offerings placed on the holy altars may bring us salvation. Through the Lord.

Almighty and merciful God, you made Saint John Mary remarkable for his pastoral zeal and his unceasing fervor in prayer and penance; grant, we ask, that through his example and intercession we may win the souls of our brothers for Christ and with them attain eternal glory. Through the same Lord.
Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. This is the priest whom the Lord has crowned. Alleluia.

Let us all rejoice in the Lord as we celebrate a feast in honor of blessed Josaphat the martyr. The angels rejoice at his martyrdom and together praise the Son of God. Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise befits the upright. ℣. Glory to the Father.

Alleluia, alleluia. V. From whatever distress they cry to me, I will hear them, and I will always be their protector. Alleluia. V. Joseph, grant us to lead an innocent life, and may it always be safe under your protection. Alleluia.

God, through Saint Joseph, your Confessor, you were pleased to provide new assistance to your Church for educating the young in a spirit of understanding and piety; grant, we ask, that through his example and intercession we may act and teach in such a way as to attain eternal rewards. Through our Lord.

Lord God, kindly receive our gifts, whose wondrous mystery Saint Justin the Martyr staunchly defended against the slanders of the ungodly. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

God, for every arduous undertaking for the glory of your name and the salvation of souls, you bestowed on blessed Lawrence, your Confessor and Doctor, the spirit of wisdom and fortitude: grant us, in that same spirit, both to know what we should do and, through his intercession, to carry out what we have recognized. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that just as blessed Louis, your Confessor, spurned the world's pleasures and sought to please only Christ the King, so his prayer may make us acceptable to you. Through the same Lord.

Lord Jesus Christ, who wonderfully revealed the unfathomable riches of your Heart to blessed Margaret Mary, virgin, grant us, through her merits and by imitating her, that, loving you in all things and above all things, we may be worthy to have a lasting home in that same Heart of yours: who live and reign with God the Father in unity.

May the gifts of your people be acceptable to you, Lord; and grant that the divine fire sent forth from the Heart of your Son, with which blessed Margaret Mary burned so intensely, may set us aflame. Through the same Lord of ours.
Hear us, O God our Savior, so that, as we rejoice in the feast of blessed Martha your Virgin, we may likewise be schooled in a spirit of reverent devotion. Through the Lord.
We ask, almighty God, that we who have received heavenly nourishment may, through the intercession of blessed Peter, your confessor, be fortified by it against every adversity. Through the Lord.
Lord, we ask that blessed Peter Chrysologus, your bishop and distinguished teacher, may come forward as an intercessor, so that your sacrifices may bring us salvation. Through the Lord.

Lord, may we never lack the devout prayer of Saint Peter Chrysologus, your bishop and teacher; may it win acceptance for our gifts and always obtain your pardon for us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you.
Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. This is the priest whom the Lord has crowned. Alleluia.

[\"s-polycarpi-episcopi-martyris\",\"mai.translation_note: Natalicia is rendered as 'birthday'; in this martyr's celebration it denotes his birth into heavenly life.

translations.text: God, you gladden us with the annual solemnity of blessed Polycarp, your martyr and bishop. Graciously grant that we who honor his birthday may also rejoice in his protection. Through our Lord.

Nourished by sharing in the sacred gift, we ask, Lord our God, that, through the intercession of blessed Polycarp, your martyr and bishop, we may experience the effect of what we celebrate in worship. Through our Lord.
Sanctify the gifts dedicated to you, Lord, and, through the intercession of blessed Polycarp, your martyr and bishop, be appeased by these same gifts and look upon us. Through our Lord.
Almighty God, look upon the sacrificial offerings we bring, and grant that we who celebrate the mysteries of the Lord's Passion may imitate what we enact. Through the same Lord.

Lord, you said, "Unless you become like little children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven." Grant us, we pray, to follow in the footsteps of Saint Thérèse the virgin in humility and simplicity of heart, so that we may attain eternal rewards, you who live and reign with God the Father in unity.
Lord, may the heavenly mystery inflame us with that fire of love by which Saint Thérèse, your virgin, devoted herself to you for humankind as a sacrificial victim of love. Through our Lord.

Lord, we pray, may the holy prayer of Saint Thérèse, your virgin, win your favor for our sacrifice, so that what is solemnly offered in her honor may be made acceptable by her merits. Through our Lord.

Hear us, God our savior, so that, just as we rejoice in the feast of blessed Teresa, your virgin, we may be nourished by the food of her heavenly teaching and be schooled in the spirit of reverent devotion. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.
Lord, so that your sacrifices may bring us salvation, we ask that blessed Thomas, your Confessor and eminent Doctor, come forward to intercede. Through our Lord.
Lord, may the devout prayer of Saint Thomas, your Confessor and Doctor, never fail us; may it make our gifts acceptable and always obtain your pardon for us. Through the Lord.
Almighty God, look upon our weakness, and since the weight of our own conduct burdens us, may the glorious intercession of blessed Timothy, your martyr and bishop, protect us. Through the Lord.

Nourished by sharing in the sacred gift, we ask, Lord our God, that, through the intercession of blessed Timothy, your martyr and bishop, we may experience the effect of what we celebrate in worship. Through our Lord.

Lord, graciously accept the sacrificial offerings dedicated to you in honor of the merits of blessed Timothy, your martyr and bishop, and grant that they may become an everlasting help to us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in unity.

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that as we give thanks for the gifts we have received, through the intercession of blessed Titus, your confessor and bishop, we may receive greater blessings. Through the Lord.
Almighty God, we ask that, through the intercession of blessed Vincent your Confessor, we who have received heavenly food may be protected by it against all adversity. Through the Lord.
Alleluia, alleluia. V. After giving birth, Virgin, you remained inviolate: Mother of God, intercede for us. Alleluia.
Blessed is the womb of the Virgin Mary, which bore the Son of the eternal Father.

Blessed and worthy of veneration are you, Virgin Mary, who, with your chastity untouched, were found to be the mother of the Savior. V. Virgin Mother of God, he whom the whole world cannot contain enclosed himself within your womb, becoming man.
Alleluia, alleluia. V. Holy Mary, Queen of heaven and Mistress of the world, stood in sorrow beside the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed are the senses of the blessed Virgin Mary, which merited the palm of martyrdom beneath the Lord’s Cross without death.

You are sorrowful and worthy of tears, Virgin Mary, standing beside the Cross of the Lord Jesus, your Son, the Redeemer. V. Virgin Mother of God, the author of life, whom the whole world cannot contain, bears this torment of the cross, having become man.
Remember, Virgin Mother of God, when you stand in the Lord’s presence, to speak for our good, so that he may turn his wrath away from us.
May our frailty be upheld by the remedies of your mercy, Lord, we ask, so that, worn down by its own condition, it may be restored by your kindness. Through our Lord.
May the feasts of the blessed martyrs and bishops Cornelius and Cyprian protect us, we pray, Lord, and may their venerable prayer commend us. Through the Lord.
Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. The army of martyrs, clothed in white, praises you, O Lord. Alleluia.

God, you gladden us with the yearly solemnity of your holy martyrs Januarius and his companions; graciously grant that we who rejoice in their merits may be set aflame by their examples. Through the Lord.
Lord, may this communion cleanse us of sin and, through the intercession of your holy martyrs Januarius and his companions, make us sharers in the heavenly remedy. Through the Lord.
Lord, we pray, be appeased by the gifts we have offered, and, through the intercession of your holy martyrs Januarius and his companions, defend us from every danger. Through the Lord.
Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. This is the true brotherhood that overcame the sins of the world: it followed Christ and, glorious, possesses the kingdoms of heaven. Alleluia.

Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. This is the true brotherhood that overcame the sins of the world: it followed Christ and, glorious, possesses the kingdoms of heaven. Alleluia. ℣. The army of martyrs, clothed in white, praises you, O Lord. Alleluia.
Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. This is the true brotherhood that overcame the sins of the world: it followed Christ and, glorious, possesses the kingdoms of heaven. Alleluia.

God, who give us joy in the solemn celebration (commemoration) of your Apostles Philip and James, grant, we ask, that we may be taught by the examples of those in whose merits we rejoice. Through our Lord.
Alleluia, alleluia. ℣. This is the true brotherhood that overcame the sins of the world: it followed Christ and, glorious, possesses the kingdoms of heaven. Alleluia.
God, whom sin offends and penance appeases, look favorably upon the prayers of your people who plead with you, and turn away the scourges of your anger that we deserve for our sins. Through the Lord.
Grant, we ask, almighty God, that with purified minds we may understand the most sacred mysteries of your Son’s Transfiguration, which we celebrate in solemn worship. Through the same Lord of ours.
Blessed is the womb of the Virgin Mary, which bore the Son of the eternal Father.

Blessed and worthy of veneration are you, Virgin Mary, who, with your virginity untouched, were found to be the Mother of the Savior. V. Virgin Mother of God, he whom the whole world cannot contain enclosed himself in your womb, having become man.
Blessed are you, Virgin Mary, who bore the Creator of all; you gave birth to him who made you, and you remain a Virgin forever.

Alleluia, alleluia. V. Christ has risen and has shone upon us, whom he redeemed with his blood. Alleluia. V. I came forth from the Father and came into the world; again I leave the world and go to the Father. Alleluia.
Alleluia, alleluia. V. Happy are you, holy Virgin Mary, and most worthy of every praise: for from you has arisen the sun of righteousness, Christ our God. Alleluia.
Blessed is the womb of the Virgin Mary, which bore the Son of the eternal Father.

Blessed and venerable are you, Virgin Mary, who were found the Savior's mother without violation of virginity. V. Virgin Mother of God, he whom the whole world cannot contain enclosed himself in your womb, made man.
Hail, holy Mother, who bore the King who rules heaven and earth for ever and ever. My heart has uttered a good word; I declare my works to the King. V. Glory to the Father.
Blessed are you, Virgin Mary, who bore the Creator of all: you brought forth him who made you, and you remain a virgin for ever.
