Each element either carries a separately identified historical witness or project study translation, or states why its words are unavailable here. The approved 2011 English is registered as restricted provenance and is not published in this tracked corpus. Historical English and new study English do not replace or clear it. The historical Latin is independently sourced ancient wording, not a reproduction of the controlling 2008 Missal. Its spelling, source extent, optional configurations and relation to the target are stated separately for each join. The repository holds a verified secondary digital 2002 Ordo and the official bounded 2008 variation list, but no complete authenticated 2008 exemplar. An uncollated relation makes no claim of complete target identity. Concise source qualifications accompany held bodies; their full evidence remains in the source notes. Proper texts belong to the day's formulary, and locally composed words have no fixed body to supply.
advisory.before: A finding aid for the shape of the rite, and never a book to celebrate from. Most of this Order of Mass is missing here, and every element says which of its two texts is missing and why, because they are not missing for one reason. The English side has six reasons. Twenty-seven elements record a rights absence rather than text on this distribution surface. Sixteen modelled elements have official exemplars registered but no tracked payload this generator may join to them. Six variable texts belong to the Propers rather than this frame. Three elements have no fixed words, three span parts with different availability, and six are prayers the Priest says quietly for which no exact exemplar is held. The Latin side has seven reasons, and they run from the reform's own new matter, which is the Holy See's and is withheld, to a rubric that has no words in any book. Where a text is missing what stands in its place is the element's received Latin incipit, which is a reference and not the prayer. THE LATIN THAT IS HERE IS NOT THIS MISSAL'S. Twenty elements carry Latin, and at every one of them it is the facing column of an 1861 Philadelphia lay hand missal printing the ancient prayer this Order of Mass received. The controlling 2008 Latin is not distributable on this surface and is not served as an element text anywhere on this page. Each of the twenty says beside its own words which prayer of that older book it is, at which printed page and leaf, which accidents of that printing it carries unnormalised, and whether its identity with the controlling edition has been established by a collation this repository holds or is so far only asserted. Five are established; fifteen are not, and they say so.

Smoothing them would manufacture a target witness this project has not established; carrying them silently under a heading naming the editio typica would attribute a lay printer's misprints to the Holy See. Naming them is the only honest third option and it is what this file does.

before.what: Four English-only orations belong to the pre-1955 second-oration regime printed bodily inside the 1861 Ordinary: a-cunctis, secreta-ii, postcommunio-mundet, and et-famulos. The 1962 Ordo Missae does not carry that regime, which the 1960 Code of Rubrics abolished. All four are excluded from this target frame (2026-10-19: the last two on the verified 1962 Ordo passages, see the conclusio exclusions); the classification remains the source-witness accounting for their missing Latin. This classification supplies no Latin body or inferred extent.

before.label: The 1861 lay witness supplies its own English heading or rubric
before.what: Seventy-one English-only blocks are the 1861 printer's own headings or rubrics for a lay reader, not untranslated Latin text: 50 rubrics and 21 headings. Eight are excluded from this target frame, leaving 63 emitted elements in this class. No Latin counterpart or prayer/rubric extent is inferred.

before.label: This day’s Ordinary appointment is not established
before.what: Nothing in this repository yet establishes which text the day appoints here: no reading of the celebrated formulary's own direction is recorded, no dated span stated by the 1962 book covers the date, and no sourced default applies. For the Preface this is now only a date the declared spans cannot be evaluated on (no civil date or year anchors reach the frame); RGMR 482's three steps are otherwise all declared: the formulary's printed direction, the de Tempore spans of RGMR 484-493 and the common default of RGMR 482 and 498. The stand-in replaces printing every Preface the witness holds, which claimed all of them were said.

before.label: The appointed Preface is absent from the 1861 witness
before.what: The day appoints a Preface the 1861 Cummiskey lay missal does not print: it knew eleven Prefaces and the 1962 Missal prints sixteen (RGMR 484-499; the Chrism Mass, Sacred Heart, Christ the King, St Joseph and the Dead). No witness this frame joins carries it, and no other Preface is shown in its place.

before.label: The appointed proper Canon form is not held here
before.what: The day appoints a proper Communicantes whose head (before the dagger at which the 1962 Canon joins every proper form to its shared continuation, printed pp. 304-305, nn. 1093-1096) no witness this frame joins prints: the 1861 Cummiskey Canon carries only the common forms (canon-missae-en seq 8 and 10), and the public-domain printings of these heads have not been collated for this surface. The common form is NOT shown in the proper head's place; the shared continuation, which is held, follows. Since 2026-10-19 the Pentecost head and the Easter and Pentecost Hanc igitur are held and no longer stand under this reason.

before.label: Held English differs from this proper Communicantes
before.what: No public-domain English this repository has read renders the head of the Pentecost Communicantes word for word. The Lasance missal (printed p. 811, passage pentecost-communicantes-and-hanc-igitur) calls the Virgin mother of 'the same' Lord, a word the Pentecost Latin does not print, and is a variant under the 2026-09-03 words rule; the 1861 Cummiskey (printed p. 377, IA leaf n385) prints only part of the head and refers the reader to its Ordinary, whose English does not mark where it resumes. No English is shown and none is composed.

before.label: Held English lacks the 1962 Saint Joseph clause
before.what: Every public-domain English this repository holds for the Communicantes passes from the Virgin to the Apostles without the clause naming Saint Joseph that the 1962 Canon prints in its continuation (decree of 13 November 1962): the 1861 Cummiskey Canon (canon-missae-en seq 8, printed p. xxxiv) and the Lasance missal (printed p. 811). Under the 2026-09-03 words rule an English lacking a clause is a variant, so it is not bound as the antecedent of the 1962 wording (roadmap, 1962 Pentecost complete-text plan). No English is shown and none is composed; the short-phrase basis for the Latin clause supplies no English.

after.label: The 1861 witness prints this block only in English
after.what: The 1861 book sets this block across the full measure in English only and prints no Latin text for it; the facing-column Latin of every block that has one is transcribed. The absence is the witness's, not a rights or effort gap. It holds for 83 elements - 53 rubrics, 21 English headings, 8 prayers (a-cunctis, munda-cor-meum, dominus-sit-in-corde-meo, per-evangelica-dicta, accendat-in-nobis, secreta-ii, postcommunio-mundet, et-famulos) and the form benedicat-vos-omnipotens-deus - and each was established by opening the leaf, not inferred: leaves n25-n56 were all read. Whether the 1920 Ordo Missae prints any of these is a separate target-edition question; the reason is scoped to this witness's page and says nothing about the rite.

after.label: This day’s Ordinary appointment is not established

A formulary's Preface is recorded only where the Bonn witness prints it (the `attested_appointments` of src/sources/calendars/roman-pre-1955/propers.yaml), and no span or default is declared: the witness's general rubrics (Additiones et variationes tit. advisory.after: A pre-1955 lay hand missal's Ordinary, and never a book to celebrate from. This is the Ordinary of the Mass as the 1861 Philadelphia printing of Eugene Cummiskey set it for the laity to follow the Mass with; the base English is that printing's own anonymous translation. The joined historical English is not an approved liturgical translation, and nothing here may be used for recitation. The book is a witness to the discipline in force before the 1955 and 1960 reforms, and it differs from the 1920 typical edition in orthography and in some rubrics. Where it prints something the 1920 Ordo Missae does not - a second collect, a second secret, devotions at the Gospel - the element says so in its own place. Both of the book's columns are now transcribed: the Latin named below is the 1861 printing's own, read from the facing column of the same openings, and it is a pre-1955 witness to the rite and never the text of the 1920 typical edition - its Communicantes prints no clause naming St Joseph, its Prefaces are the eleven this book knew, and its spelling, its j and its ae and oe ligatures are its own. Where the book sets a block across the full measure in English and prints no facing Latin at all, that silence is the witness's own and the element says so. Separately identified historical English supplies the five proper Communicantes and the Easter/Pentecost Hanc igitur, under the witness and limits stated beside each element.

The paschal substitution Concede for the seasonal orations. Established as NOT said outside the windows its rubrics name, the union of the 1861 witness's own rubrics (ordinarium-oblatio-en seq 1 and 54, ordinarium-conclusio-en seq 6: Candlemas to Passion Sunday, the third Sunday after Pentecost to Advent) and the Bonn reimpressio's Additiones et Variationes in Rubricis Missalis tit. VI n. 1 and 3) (artifact p. 56*, read at 200 dpi on 2026-10-19: 3 February to the Tuesday after Quinquagesima, the first Sunday after Pentecost to the Saturday before Advent). Inside a window it is said only in semidouble and simple offices (RG IX n. 1; tit. VI n. 1), and the rank of the day is not held here, so it stays unresolved there. Added 2026-10-19 (C2 gap G5).

The paschal substitution Concede for the seasonal orations. Established as NOT said from Passion Sunday to Saturday in albis and through the octave of Pentecost, where a single oration contra persecutores is said instead (Bonn Additiones tit. VI n. 1 and 6), artifact pp. 56*-57*), and on the vigil of Pentecost, which omits the seasonal orations (tit. VI n. 1; Proprium printed p. 399). Elsewhere the rank of the day decides and it stays unresolved. Added 2026-10-19 (C2 gap G5).

after.caution: The Latin of a pre-1955 lay hand missal's facing column: never an altar book, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
